request.spec:
A claim now has a status. It starts as DRAFT; it can be opened (OPEN) and then settled
(SETTLED); a DRAFT or OPEN claim can be voided (VOID). A SETTLED or VOID claim cannot change
status, and the buttons for a change that is not allowed are refused with an error on the claim.
Only OPEN and SETTLED claims count toward claimed, due-total and every total; drafts and voided
claims do not. Show each claim's status. Every status change writes an audit line: CLAIM_OPENED,
CLAIM_SETTLED or CLAIM_VOIDED, each with person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A claim now has a status. It starts as DRAFT; it can be opened (OPEN) and then settled
(SETTLED); a DRAFT or OPEN claim can be voided (VOID). A SETTLED or VOID claim cannot change
status, and the buttons for a change that is not allowed are refused with an error on the claim.
Only OPEN and SETTLED claims count toward claimed, due-total and every total; drafts and voided
claims do not. Show each claim's status. Every status change writes an audit line: CLAIM_OPENED,
CLAIM_SETTLED or CLAIM_VOIDED, each with person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claims now have a status, and all 4 Playwright tests pass when run with `bin/e2e`.

- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V7__claim_status.sql`, adds a `status` column to claims. It defaults to `DRAFT`, and a check constraint limits it to DRAFT, OPEN, SETTLED or VOID.
- **Server:**
  - A new `ClaimStatus` enum holds the allowed moves: DRAFT→OPEN, OPEN→SETTLED, and DRAFT or OPEN→VOID.
  - The new `ClaimService.changeStatus` endpoint (`PUT …/claims/{id}/status`) refuses any other move with a 409 and writes nothing, so it leaves no audit line either.
  - An allowed move writes `CLAIM_OPENED`, `CLAIM_SETTLED` or `CLAIM_VOIDED` with `person=`, `amount=` and `date=`.
  - The claim data sent to the screen now includes the status.
- **Front end:**
  - Each claim row shows its status (`claim-status`) and has Open, Settle and Void buttons.
  - A refused move shows `claim-error` on that claim. The error goes away when you take the next action on that row.
  - The person's claimed and due-total, and both sheet totals, count only OPEN and SETTLED claims.

Two things you might not expect:
- The Open, Settle and Void buttons are always shown and clickable, even when the move isn't allowed. That's deliberate: the test clicks a disallowed button and expects the error, so hiding or disabling the buttons would break it.
- A claim's own due amount still shows for draft and voided claims (a voided 30.00 claim shows 3.00 due). The test expects this; those claims are just left out of every total.

Editing a claim's amount, date or note still works in any status, including SETTLED and VOID, because the test edits a settled claim and expects that to succeed.
